text:
The Capitals are 10-6-0 while Alex Ovechkin has had one of the quietest starts of his career: one goal through his first 15 games, as Daily Faceoff noted, and 3 points in his last 10 against 4.8 expected. The off-ice story is louder. A protest is planned in Ottawa over his support for Vladimir Putin, and Ovechkin answered it in a way RG.org headlined as "Nobody's Using Me."

Tom Wilson is in the headlines too, after a boarding hit on Florida's Sandis Vilmanis got him ejected but drew no suspension. He has one point in his last 10 against 5.5 expected. Two of the team's identity players are cold, and Washington is still winning, which says something good about the rest of the lineup.

Much of that is new. Alex Tuch, whose exit from Buffalo has turned messy in public, plays on the one line that has stayed intact through recent shuffles, with Dylan Strome and Jordan Kyrou. The Boone Jenner, Justin Sourdif and Ryan Leonard group has allowed almost nothing.

The overall picture is a coin flip: 50% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and our numbers have the Caps about two and a half points ahead of what they deserved. The power play generates only half a goal of expected offense a game, and they take more penalties than they draw. The playoff odds are 64% in our simulations. What to watch: Ovechkin's finishing. If it returns to normal, this team has room to grow.
headline: Washington wins while its stars go quiet
